- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 2024 (Jan–Feb), especially after recent spikes; adjust downward bias for low volatility periods.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 75–80+), model overreacts and overshoots, then fails to correct — reduce forecast peak height by 5–10% post-spike.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: forecasts drift downward too quickly after high values; slow decay by 1–2 days post-peak.
- In mid-2024 (May), model overestimates prices by 5–15% across all periods — likely due to ignoring supply/demand shocks or policy changes; apply downward correction based on 30-day moving average of true values.
- Forecast horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are too optimistic in low-volatility regimes; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to 14-day moving average of true values.
